title: The Morning Brief: Carse Out of Second Test as England Discipline Recurs
dek: England removed fast bowler Brydon Carse from its squad for the second Test against Pakistan after he was filmed in handcuffs outside a Derby bar, with accounts differing on whether it was August 22 or August 23.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Carse becomes the third England player benched this summer for a disciplinary issue, and the Cricket Regulator's investigation, not the squad removal itself, will determine what comes next.
bottom_line: England removed fast bowler Brydon Carse from its squad for the second Test against Pakistan after he was filmed in handcuffs outside a bar in Derby, becoming the third England player benched this summer for a disciplinary breach, while the Cricket Regulator opened a formal investigation. Elsewhere, snooker's Graeme Dott was found guilty of child sexual abuse spanning 1993 to 2010, with sentencing set for 29 September, and a courtside confrontation between Enes Kanter Freedom and Natasha Cloud at a WNBA game reopened tension over the league's transgender eligibility rule. The honest read is that today's sourcing establishes the actions taken, squad removal, an ejection, a conviction, but not the fuller reasoning or outcomes behind several of them, including whether other England figures face scrutiny and what the Astros' front-office change actually involved. On the field, Miyu Yamashita tied the LPGA's 72-hole scoring record, and the Vuelta a Espana's third stage was abandoned mid-race due to hail. The coming days bring the Cricket Regulator's findings, Dott's September sentencing, and confirmation of the Astros' general manager situation as the next checkpoints.
body: The clearest thread through today's stories is discipline and process: cricket's Cricket Regulator opening an investigation into an England bowler, snooker's governing body revoking a convicted champion's membership, and a WNBA courtside confrontation testing what leagues do when tension spills onto the floor.

Brydon Carse has been removed from England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan following a police incident outside a bar in Derby. The reporting carries two dates for the incident itself, with one account citing August 22 and another citing the night of August 23, 2026; both agree Carse was filmed in handcuffs, that he was released without charge or de-arrested after agreeing to leave the area, and that the England and Wales Cricket Board referred the matter to the Cricket Regulator, which has opened an investigation. Carse becomes the third England player benched this summer for a disciplinary breach. Sonny Baker, who won his only Test cap in June against New Zealand, has been named as his replacement. Separately, the Kanter Freedom ejection from Sunday's Chicago Sky versus Indiana Fever game centers on WNBA eligibility rules for transgender athletes; Kanter Freedom, wearing a shirt reading "WOMAN noun. Adult human female," stepped toward the court after Sky guard Natasha Cloud pointed and shouted at him during a timeout, and was escorted out by security.

On the results side, Miyu Yamashita shot 23-under 257 to win the CPKC Women's Open by nine shots, tying the LPGA Tour's 72-hole scoring record set by Kim Sei-young in 2018, and the Vuelta a Espana's third stage was abandoned with 15km remaining after severe hailstorms in the French Pyrenees, with organizers declaring no stage winner. On the business and personnel side, ESPN announced RedZone at the US Open, the first non-football use of the brand it secured through its NFL equity deal, debuting August 30, while Karl Ravech called his final ESPN broadcast on August 24 after 33 years, having been laid off in July but retained for contracted summer dates. MLB.com is reported to have carried a story that Dana Brown and the Houston Astros parted ways as general manager, though the underlying article could not be verified and no details on timing or succession are confirmed. Snooker's Graeme Dott, the 2006 World Snooker Championship winner, was found guilty of two counts of lewd and libidinous behaviour spanning 1993 to 2010, with sentencing set for 29 September in Edinburgh; the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association has permanently revoked his membership. And rugby league mourns Sir Billy Boston, the first player knighted in the sport's 130-year history, who died aged 92 weeks after receiving his knighthood from King Charles.

On why these things happened, the reporting is explicit in some cases and silent in others. Carse's removal follows a captain's recent call for improved behavior, per the reporting, making this the third such benched player this summer, though the reporting does not say whether Ben Stokes or another named figure faces investigation themselves. The Kanter Freedom incident is tied directly to unresolved tension over the WNBA's transgender eligibility rule. Dott's conviction follows a 2001 police contact that produced no charges at the time, a gap the reporting flags without further explanation. The Astros story offers no reasoning at all, since the underlying report could not be verified.
Desk boards were not available this run, so today's picture rests entirely on the desk's published reporting.

In the coming days, watch the Cricket Regulator's investigation into Carse for any findings beyond squad removal, and whether his absence proves precautionary or longer. Watch for an official WNBA statement on the Kanter Freedom ejection. Watch Dott's 29 September sentencing in Edinburgh. Watch whether Vuelta organizers can resume normal racing on stage four after Monday's weather disruption. Watch for confirmation of the Dana Brown-Astros terms from the club or MLB directly, and whether ESPN names on-air talent for its RedZone at the US Open coverage before its August 30 debut.
